players.product: Susquehanna nuclear + PJM baseload gas generation contracted to data centers (Amazon ~2 GW PPA, powered-land sites)

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $374 million and adjusted free cash flow of $212 million ($847 million and $562 million year to date); results 'substantially higher' than a year ago, driven by the Freedom and Guernsey plants, higher PJM capacity pricing, higher generation volumes from Susquehanna and the fossil fleet, and 'the AWS contract, which continues to ramp'.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 adj EBITDA $374 million; adj FCF $212 million; YTD $847 million / $562 million

quarterly_data.signal: Closed the Cornerstone acquisition in June — the Waterford, Darby and Lawrenceburg plants bring over two and a half gigawatts of natural gas-fired generation into the portfolio 'just in time for the peak summer demand'; fleet generated approximately 30 TWh at a 51% capacity factor, 14 percentage points higher than the prior year.
quarterly_data.figure: over 2.5 GW gas generation added; ~30 TWh generated; 51% capacity factor

quarterly_data.signal: Raised 2026 guidance to adjusted EBITDA of $2.025 billion-$2.225 billion and adjusted free cash flow of $1.2 billion-$1.35 billion (includes Cornerstone); now exceeding the ~$2.6 billion pro forma 2027 EBITDA indicated in January; 2027 base-case free cash flow outlook $34 per share rising to $40 per share in 2028 (approximately $37 a share and $48 a share after buybacks); ~$4 billion of adjusted free cash flow expected through 2028 with at least 70%, $2.8 billion, returned via buybacks.

Powered-land pipeline: 'approximately four gigawatts of advantage data center sites with utility load commitments' offering speed to market (organic sites adjacent to generation plus acquired sites), and '2+ GW of new build capacity projects backed with interconnection queue positions' (batteries, peakers, uprates). Customer universe for long-term PPAs is 'expanding beyond hyperscalers to include co-locators, neoclouds, and even large C&I customers'; hybrid structure pairs existing baseload energy with new capacity.
quarterly_data.figure: ~4 GW of data-center sites with utility load commitments; 2+ GW new-build capacity pipeline

quarterly_data.signal: Contracted-margin path: as the AWS campus ramps to full build-out (projected between 2028 and 2030) long-term contracted margin rises from 10% to 35% of gross margin, making contracted margin with a double-A counterparty the largest revenue stream; an additional approximately 2 GW of long-term contracts on similar terms could take long-term contracts to 60% of the gross margin mix beyond 2030. Acceleration of the existing 2 GW PPA or new data center PPAs 'could add 10% or more' to the cash flow profile each.
quarterly_data.figure: contracted margin 10% -> 35% by 2030; potential 60% with another ~2 GW of PPAs

quarterly_data.signal: PJM fundamentals: 'nearly 50% increase in West Hub sparks since last year'; 2028 PPL spark spreads up 28% and ADHUB up 27% versus July 2025 pricing; long-term hyperscaler PPAs were recently discussed at prices in the $80 per MWh range and forward wholesale energy plus capacity is now approaching or exceeding those levels; the last three base residual capacity auctions cleared at the price cap with uncapped prices that would have settled in excess of $500 a MWd; bilateral capacity bids at the cap seen for the early 2030s. PPL basis widened from ~$9 per megawatt hour historically to approximately $20 per MWh on transmission outages — every $1 improvement in basis equals approximately $1 of adjusted FCF per share.
quarterly_data.figure: West Hub sparks +~50% YoY; 2028 PPL sparks +28%; capacity auctions clearing at cap (uncapped >$500/MWd)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO on hyperscaler timing: 'Hyperscalers right now are all looking for something that can be done exactly in 2028. We already did that... It's being built out at the Susquehanna Campus'; hyperscalers 'are all spending $50 billion a year' deciding where to put chips down for 2027-2028 before turning to 2029 — new PPAs are 'a matter of when, not if'. Talen will not do behind-the-meter; front-of-the-meter grid-connected hybrid solutions 'beat any new build CCGT and any behind-the-meter solution on a total cost'.

Next catalysts: formal 2027 guidance plus 2028 and 2029 outlooks on the third quarter call; Talen plans to participate in PJM's Reliability Backstop Procurement (RBP, targeted to be finalized at FERC by September 29th, with a 555 soft cap) with uprates, batteries and peakers, and PJM's IRAS (connect-and-manage) proposal was due the same week.

connects_to.relationship: long-term nuclear PPA — Susquehanna campus power supply to AWS data centers (~2 GW)

contracts.signal: Existing 'nearly two-gigawatt contract ramps through 2030'; the AWS campus adjacent to Susquehanna is projected to reach full build-out sometime between 2028 and 2030, at which point long-term contracted margin rises from 10% to 35% and contracted gross margin with a double-A credit counterparty becomes Talen's largest revenue stream. The AWS contract 'continues to ramp' and contributed to Q2 EBITDA; acceleration of the 2 GW PPA is cited as an upside lever worth 10% or more of cash flow.
contracts.date_signed: not stated (existing PPA; campus sold to AWS)
